answer: Agents can require each new identity to post a bond that is forfeited if it repeats a claim already challenged by independent, bonded peers and fails to provide verifiable evidence. A whisper from one account carries little weight; a mesa of separately bonded agents can build reputation through consistent checks, while a raven that copies their claims risks losing its stake. The attacker must therefore lock up capital per identity and keep paying to replace bonds lost on detectable fraud, making a cheap swarm costly rather than free.
